questions.question: As systems scale, Xu emphasizes adding operational tooling such as:
options: Deleting logs so disks stay empty during incidents.
Logging, metrics, and automation to run the system.
Manual SSH only with no metrics ever collected.
Disabling alerts so on-call never wakes up.

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: Logging, metrics, automation When working with a small website that runs on a few servers, logging, metrics, and automation support are good practices but not a necessity.

questions.question: Architecture fitness functions (FSA) help architects:
options: Avoid verifying that teams follow decisions.
Measure compliance with architecture characteristics automatically.
Replace all production monitoring with slideware.
Ban metrics because they encourage premature optimization.
questions.explanation: measuring compliance using automated fitness functions

reference.book: Fundamentals of Software Architecture, 2nd Edition by Mark Richards and Neal Ford
reference.excerpt: The book Building Evolutionary Architectures (O’Reilly, 2022) by Neal Ford et al. describes a family of techniques called fitness functions used to automate many aspects of architecture governance.

questions.question: True or false: Without monitoring, you cannot tell whether scalability or reliability goals are actually met.

questions.question: Good alerts should primarily fire on:
options: Every debug log line in development laptops.
User-visible symptoms (errors, latency, saturation) that need action.
Successful health checks that return 200 OK continuously.
CDN cache hits for static logo images only.

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: Logging: Monitoring error logs is important because it helps to identify errors and problems in the system.

questions.question: Correlation IDs in logs help you:
options: Hide the path of a request across services during an incident.
Trace one request across services when diagnosing failures.
Encrypt the database by renaming columns randomly.
Increase QPS without adding any capacity.

reference.book: System Design Interview – An Insider's Guide by Alex Xu
reference.excerpt: The interactions between an interviewer and a candidate help to clarify the type of rate limiters we are trying to build.
